prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1364; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a rear-end collision at a signalized intersection. Insured vehicle struck claimant's vehicle from behind at low speed. Police report obtained and reviewed. Liability appears probable against insured pending scene photos and driver statement.

Entry 2: Claimant reports wrist fracture sustained in the impact and has been placed in a splint by treating physician. Claimant is now represented by counsel, who has requested that all further contact be routed through their office. Letter of representation received and logged.

Entry 3: Insured's recorded statement taken. Insured acknowledges following too closely and states the brake lights on claimant's vehicle came on late. Rear bumper damage on claimant's vehicle confirmed from photos. Subrogation notice to be sent to insured's carrier if applicable.

Entry 4: Medical records requested from claimant's counsel, including emergency department intake, imaging reports for the wrist, and orthopedic follow-up notes. Counsel has indicated surgical consultation is being considered. Reserve for bodily injury reviewed and increased to reflect fracture severity.

Entry 5: Demand package received from claimant's counsel with supporting medical bills and wage loss documentation. Demand under review by claims supervisor. Counter-evaluation to be prepared once treatment status is confirmed. Follow-up diary set to check on claimant's recovery progress and any further procedures.
